title: Stage-discharge rating at the Missouri River at Hermann
summary: A gage reads the stage; a rating curve fitted to field measurements turns it into discharge. The curve moves as the bed changes and is least known at the floods it matters most for.

concepts.label: Stream gage
concepts.description: USGS 06934500, Missouri River at Hermann, MO: a stage sensor and the section where flow is measured.

facts.text: Hermann is the last USGS gage on the Missouri before it joins the Mississippi, draining about 522,500 square miles.

children.label: Stage
children.description: Gage height in ft above the gage datum, recorded continuously.

children.label: Gage datum
children.description: The reference level stages are read from; a change shifts every stage.

concepts.label: Field measurement
concepts.description: A hydrographer's discharge measurement (current meter or ADCP across the section) with the stage read at the time.

children.label: Hysteresis
children.description: On a rising flood the water surface is steeper and the same stage carries more water than on the falling limb.

concepts.label: Rating curve
concepts.description: Q = C (h − e)^b, fitted to the field measurements; turns every stage reading into a discharge.

facts.text: USGS computes streamflow from stage through ratings developed from discharge measurements, with shifts applied between measurements.

children.label: Hydraulic control
children.description: What sets the stage: a section control (riffle, weir, b ≈ 1.5–2.5) or the channel's friction (Manning, b ≈ 5/3 for a wide channel).

children.label: Rating shift
children.description: The curve moving with scour, fill, vegetation or dredging; seen as residuals drifting by decade.

children.label: Extrapolation
children.description: The curve above the highest measured stage; where the equally good curves (e in its 95% interval) disagree most.

concepts.label: Annual flood peak
concepts.description: Each water year's highest discharge and its stage, as published.

children.label: Flood frequency
children.description: The 100-year flood: the discharge exceeded with 1% chance a year, fitted to the annual peaks (Bulletin 17C, log-Pearson III).

children.label: Historic flood
children.description: Peaks before systematic gaging (1844, 1903), estimated from flood marks.

concepts.label: Channel change
concepts.description: Bed degradation of the lower Missouri from commercial sand dredging and sediment trapped behind upstream dams.
